applicability: Forge/GT shaped or shapeless crafting input originally specified as oredict:craftingTool*
Chosen concrete item is gregtech:gt.metatool.01* / MetaGeneratedTool
Not an arbitrary machine input containing a tool, and not every item in the ore dictionary group
selectedInputRule.meaning: One usable reusable tool must exist before crafting. It is returned with wear; it is neither a fresh consumed item per operation nor an immortal catalyst.
preserveFields: current and maximum durability when known
selectedInputRule.noGlobalMutation: Do not set consumed:false on an entire craftingTool group, because disposable variants share those groups.

fullAtlasGroupRule.annotation: Herramienta requerida; la variante GT normal se devuelve con desgaste. Algunas alternativas Single Use se consumen. Consultar variante y NBT.
fullAtlasGroupRule.candidateOverrides: Default selection preference only; do not remove alternatives.

units.GTToolDamage: The listed wear values use internal GT.ToolStats damage units. doDamageToItem converts vanilla damage to GT units with factor100; getContainerItem uses internal units directly.
units.ordinaryFreshToolLifetime: Requires chosen NBT maxDamage,currentDamage and break behavior. No exact replacement count has been calculated here.
units.electricTools: Different power and probabilistic durability behavior; excluded from ordinary-tool wear lifetime assumptions.

verifiedBehavior: Crafting container callback copies one tool, applies the tool-stat crafting damage, and returns the remaining stack.
Usable tools with valid stats report a container item; the container stays in the crafting grid.
Non-electric tools accumulate GT durability damage; on reaching maximum damage they may become a broken item or be removed.
Electric variants consume their power and only sometimes accumulate durability damage; do not apply the ordinary-tool lifetime formula to them.
Lowercase recipe characters map to ore dictionary craftingTool groups, including saw, file, screwdriver, hard hammer and wire cutter.
These groups can accept different item classes; group membership alone does not establish reusable-tool semantics.
GGFab single-use variants are assigned the same craftingTool dictionary groups as normal GT tools.
Their enum contains independent mold/item IDs, so a full-group alternative list includes disposable variants.
Single-use item family uses a different item implementation from MetaGeneratedTool; do not apply its container callback by ore dictionary group alone.
